<u>Water Quality</u> - Agricultural activities and overgrazing almost certainly constitute a major source of suspended sediment in surface water. Residues of agricultural chemicals such as fertilizers and biocides may also enter surface water.
Low level pollution sources within the Project Area include organic contributions from plants and domestic and wild animals (living and dead) and inorganic contribution from the weathering and erosion of soils, unconsolidated material, and rocks. There is little or no contribution from domestic wastes in the general Project Area. Algal growth, decaying vegetation and occasional intensive growth of water plants tend to alter the water quality of stock ponds and ponced areas of streams (U.S. Bureau of Indian Affairs, 1975, p. 136). An impoundment below SW-6 on Plum Creek exhibits high-intensity growth of water plants (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 1).
The only industrial development in the Project Area is the surface coal mine located on Tract III. Alkar he mine drainage waters characterized by high dissolved solids concentrations and suspended sediment are typical potential pollution sources. Miscellaneous low level sources may include wastewater from domestic and industrial sources, by-products of material buried in sanitary landfills, and organic residues dispersed by heavy machinery, vehicles, and railroad equipment.
